A.explanation: This is $800 \text{ N} \times 40.0 \text{ m s}^{-1} = 32 \text{ kW}$. It keeps the resistive force at 800 N and ignores that force is proportional to $v^2$.

B.explanation: This uses a doubled force of $1600 \text{ N}$ times $40.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$. It assumes force is proportional to $v$, not to $v^2$.

C.explanation: Doubling $v$ makes $F$ increase by $2^2 = 4$ to $3200 \text{ N}$, so $P = 3200 \times 40.0 = 128000 \text{ W} = 128 \text{ kW}$.

D.explanation: This corresponds to a force of $12800 \text{ N}$. It applies the $v^2$ factor twice instead of once when scaling from $20.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $40.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

hints: Notice the resistive force at $20.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ is $800 \text{ N}$, but the speed doubles to $40.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $F$ is proportional to $v^2$, not to $v$.
Recall that steady speed means driving force equals resistive force, and useful power is $P = Fv$ with $F$ evaluated at $40.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
First find the new resistive force using the ratio $(40.0/20.0)^2$, then multiply that force by $40.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and convert $\text{W}$ to $\text{kW}$.
walkthrough: For steady speed the engine driving force must balance the resistive force, so first find the resistive force at $40.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Write $F = kv^2$. Speed increases by factor $40.0/20.0 = 2$, so $F$ increases by factor $2^2 = 4$.
Useful output power at constant velocity is $P = Fv$. So $P = 3200 \text{ N} \times 40.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Calculate $P = 128000 \text{ W} = 128 \text{ kW}$. This checks as $\text{N} \times \text{m s}^{-1} = \text{W}$. This is option C.
